Shows your aircraft on an offline world map during a flight, with distance flown and remaining, speed, altitude, time to go and arrival time. It needs no network, no account and no server. Position comes from the phone\'s GPS when it can see satellites; otherwise the aircraft is moved along the planned route by time and speed.

Choose origin and destination by IATA code (TLV, LHR) or by city / airport name in English. Fastest: tap "Scan boarding pass" and point the camera at the barcode, or pick a screenshot of the pass; origin, destination and flight number are read from it. The scheduled departure time is optional and is used only when no GPS fix is available. Tap "Start flight". Return here any time with the aircraft button to correct the plan or end the flight.

Eye button: visual fix \u2014 pick a city or place you can see out of the window, the side and a rough distance; the aircraft is moved along the route accordingly (about 15 km accuracy, useful only without GPS). + / \u2212 zoom (also pinch or double-tap). Frame button: show the whole route. Target button: centre on the aircraft. Compass / aircraft button: north-up or track-up. GPS button: switch between live tracking and estimate-only. Dragging the map pauses following for 20 seconds. The bottom panel expands on tap.

In Settings you can download once (on Wi-Fi, about 60\u201380 MB) the NASA Blue Marble satellite mosaic (public domain) and show it under the lines and labels. Resolution is about 1 km per pixel, matching what is visible from cruise altitude: mountains, coasts, deserts, lakes. This is the only download the app ever makes; in flight everything is local.

Dashed line: the remaining planned route. Solid orange line: the part already flown. Faint dotted line: the original plan, shown only after the route has been re-planned. Turquoise line: the actual measured track, shown only after a proven deviation. Shaded band: the along-route uncertainty of the position.

Tracking: a GPS fix arrived within the last 10 seconds. Route estimate: GPS lost; the aircraft moves along the route at the last known speed, blending toward a typical cruise speed, and the uncertainty band grows about 3 % of the distance per second without a fix. Predicted only: no fix ever received; position follows a standard climb / cruise / descent profile from the takeoff time. Estimate only: you switched sensors off deliberately.

\u25CF measured now. \u25D0 fused: measured recently and propagated. \u25CB predicted from the route and time. \u25CC stale: the last measurement is old. The aircraft icon is solid when the position is measured or fused and hollow when it is predicted.
Why the aircraft stays on the route

The planned route is treated as the strongest information. A single or weak GPS fix cannot pull the aircraft off it; it only moves the aircraft along it. A measured lateral offset is shown as a number ("not yet confirmed"). When at least 6 good fixes over 3 minutes agree on an offset of 15 km or more, with a heading that disagrees with the route, the deviation is accepted: the route is re-planned from the proven position to the destination, the old plan is drawn faintly and the real track is drawn in turquoise. Near the destination (last 60 km) every good fix re-anchors, because approaches never follow the direct line.

Turn on "Estimate only" in the setup screen, or tap the GPS button on the map. The phone\'s sensors are ignored and the aircraft is placed where a flight with that departure time should be (departure + 15 minutes taxi, then a standard profile). Use it to follow a flight you are not on. A scheduled time later than now is assumed to be yesterday\'s departure.
Getting a GPS fix on board

Hold the phone against the window or on the tray table next to it. The first fix after takeoff can take 30\u201360 seconds. Aisle and middle seats often get no fix at all; the app then says "Predicted only" and works from time. Fewer than 4 satellites give no position; the status shows the count so you know the receiver is alive. Airplane mode does not affect GPS.

Remaining and flown distance are measured along the route. Time to go assumes cruise speed plus 20 minutes for descent. Arrival time is shown in the destination\'s local time; the panel also shows local time at origin, UTC and destination. Altitude comes from GPS only; the phone\'s barometer measures cabin pressure, which is used solely to detect climb and descent. Heading after GPS loss follows the gyroscope for 90 seconds, then the route course.

When enabled in Settings, each live flight writes a CSV file on this phone (Android/data/com.galker.flightinfo/files/logs) with the estimate and the raw GPS, barometer and gyroscope readings, once per second. Nothing is uploaded. "Share latest log" sends the file through any app you choose; a real flight log is the best way to calibrate the estimator.

Without GPS the aircraft follows the direct route; real routing may differ by hundreds of kilometres for weather or airspace, and the app cannot know until GPS returns. No flight-number lookup: there is no free offline schedule database, hence the boarding-pass scan. Local time at the current position is shown as UTC. The Earth is modelled as a sphere (0.3 % distance error).
Identify something you can see out of the window. Rough accuracy \u00B115 km; useful only when there is no GPS.

Needs internet. The first time, Android asks you to allow installing apps from FlightInfo; Play Protect may show a warning for a sideloaded app. Your settings and flight are kept.
